description: A folder of GoPro clips (already copied off the camera's SD card, or a mounted card itself) with real GPS/g-sensor telemetry embedded in each MP4's own GPMF ('GoPro Metadata Format') data stream - not a sidecar file the way BlackVue's .gps/.3gf are. Structurally close to the plain 'folder' adapter (recursive scan, no camera-specific config snapshot, no multi-direction video) but with real telemetry capability, so it gets its own manifest + GPMF-parsing code hooks rather than being force-fit into folder's capabilities:false-everywhere shape. See docs/CAMERA_ADAPTERS.md's 'Adapter families' section for why, and unsupported_notes below for what's still deliberately not offered.
unsupported_notes: GPMF's own fix-type/precision fields (GPSF/GPSP) are used only to mark a fix invalid (no lock) the way BlackVue's NMEA mode indicator is - not surfaced as separate accuracy data.

Chaptered (>4GB) recordings split by the camera across multiple files (e.g. GH010001.MP4 + GH020001.MP4) aren't stitched back into one recording - each chapter is its own recording, the same limitation FolderAdapter already has for any multi-part video today.
No 360/dual-lens (GoPro MAX-style) support - single video track per recording only, same as FolderAdapter.
No config.ini equivalent: trip gap threshold always uses default_trip_gap_seconds (300s) instead of a per-camera auto-derived nominal segment length.
No Event/Manual/Parking distinction: no --mode filtering, no --include-parking skip-and-replace, no max_parking_duration cap - every file is just 'a video'.

No live camera connection: bv-config's endpoint setup, bv-gps, and bv-live are not applicable to this adapter and shouldn't be offered for it - a GoPro has no network CGI protocol to speak to. bv-download's --media file-import mode IS applicable, though: it copies files off a mounted card without needing any live connection at all, recognizing this adapter's own video_extensions by extension (not a filename convention - GoPro's own on-camera names carry no timestamp) with each matched file's capture time coming from its mtime rather than its name.

Thumbnails are generated on demand via an ffmpeg frame-grab, not read from GoPro's own same-stem .THM sidecar (present on-camera but not confirmed to survive a plain file copy) - revisit once real footage confirms it's there.

Timestamp comes from ffprobe's embedded creation_time metadata, falling back to file mtime - GoPro's own on-camera filenames (e.g. GH010001.MP4) carry a chapter+file counter, not a timestamp, so unlike BlackVue there's no filename-based source to prefer.
